cards.explanation: The answer is True. The disciples are together with the doors locked for fear of the Jews, and Jesus came and stood among them anyway. The text doesn't tell us how He got in, so I'm not going to guess. I just know a locked door was no problem for Him, friends.

The answer is His hands and His side. After He greets them, Jesus shows the disciples His hands and His side. Those are where the nails and the wound were, and Thomas will bring them up again in a bit. Stay tuned, friends, because that detail matters later.

The answer is rejoiced! The text says the disciples rejoiced when they saw the Lord. They were together with the doors locked for fear of the Jews, and then they saw Him and rejoiced. I think that joy changed the whole feel of that room.

The answer is False. Right after the second greeting of peace, Jesus says, “As the Father has sent Me, so also I am sending you.” That's about sending, and the text gives no word about staying hidden. I think that was quite a thing to hear with the doors locked, friends.

The answer is the Holy Spirit. Jesus breathes on them and says, “Receive the Holy Spirit.” The Holy Spirit is God's own Spirit, and Jesus is the one giving this gift. I think that breath is a moment worth slowing down for, bakers.
The answer is forgiven. Jesus says, “If you forgive anyone his sins, they are forgiven…” It's a big thing to say to the disciples. I'd say they stood a little taller hearing it, friends.

The answer is False. Thomas, one of the Twelve, hears the other disciples say, “We have seen the Lord!” But he replies, “Unless I see the nail marks in His hands, and put my finger where the nails have been, and put my hand into His side, I will never believe.” His answer comes with conditions about seeing and touching, friends.

The answer is to see and touch His wounds. Thomas, one of the Twelve, says, “Unless I see the nail marks in His hands, and put my finger where the nails have been, and put my hand into His side, I will never believe.” That's a long order, friends, with seeing and touching both on it. I think Thomas had thought it all the way through.

The answer is doubting. Jesus says, “Stop doubting and believe.” Thomas had said he would never believe, and now Jesus speaks right to that. It's a straight word from the Lord, and I think Thomas knew it, friends.
The answer is “My Lord and my God!” That's what Thomas says to Jesus. After everything he said he needed, those are his words. It's quite a thing for him to say out loud, friends.

The answer is False. Jesus says, “blessed are those who have not seen and yet have believed.” So the blessing isn't only for people who saw Him. It reaches past that room, friends. That's good news for anybody who hasn't seen Him with their own eyes.

The answer is True, bakers. The writer says Jesus performed many other signs in the presence of His disciples, and they are not written in this book. Not everything He did made it onto the page. It sure makes me curious what else there was.

The answer is so you may believe and have life. The writer says these are written “…so that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and that by believing you may have life in His name.” It's written for the one reading, and that means you, friends. You've been baking right in the middle of it.
